content:
h07.

**Serving path: `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar` — avatar bytes come out of the `user.avatar_url` column (a base64 data URI), not from attachment/blob storage.**

Hops, browser → data layer:

- `FileServerService.RegisterRoutes` (route binding, `/file` group + `/users/:identifier/avatar`) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-124 (full path confirmed by server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go:527)
- `FileServerService.serveUserAvatar` (the serving handler) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168
- `Profile.AllowAnonymous` (gate: private instance requires a viewer) — internal/profile/profile.go:46
- `FileServerService.getCurrentUser` → `Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser` (only on the private-instance branch) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:708 → server/auth/authenticator.go:190
- `FileServerService.getUserByUsername` (builds `store.FindUser{Username: &identifier}` — this is where "another user" is resolved) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715
- `Store.GetUser` (cache hit only when looked up by ID, so a username lookup always falls through) — store/user.go:148
- `Store.ListUsers` (populates `userCache` via `cache.Cache.Set`) — store/user.go:136, store/cache/cache.go:93
- `Driver.ListUsers` (storage interface boundary) — store/driver.go:47
- `DB.ListUsers` — `SELECT … avatar_url … FROM user WHERE username = ?` — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88 (peers: store/db/postgres/user.go, store/db/mysql/user.go)
- `user.avatar_url` column (stored data) — store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:20

Response side, after the data returns:

- `FileServerService.parseDataURI` (splits the stored `data:` URI into MIME type + decoded bytes) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737
- type allow-list `avatarAllowedTypes`, then `setSecurityHeaders` + `c.Blob` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:201-209, :758

Two notes on the boundary: the frontend `UserAvatar` component renders whatever `avatarUrl` the API returned (web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx:14) — I found no client code constructing `/file/users/.../avatar` (searched 433 files under web/src), so that endpoint is consumed by direct URL references (e.g. RSS/OG markup or stored avatar URLs) rather than by the avatar component. Also, unlike `serveAttachmentFile`, this handler has no per-user visibility check beyond the anonymous gate — any authenticated viewer (or anyone, on a public instance) can fetch any username's avatar.
